extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers preparing an NIH R21 grant application (applicants and institutional grants administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A filled NIH R21 (Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant Program) sample application showing required SF424/R&R and PHS 398 components, project narrative, facilities, equipment, vertebrate animal justification, biosketches, resource sharing, and experimental design. Useful as a model for preparing R21 submissions in biomedical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA instructions / application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and FOIA / confidentiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the application is copyrighted; the awardee provided express permission for NIAID to post this grant application and summary statement for educational purposes, with attribution requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the material (e.g., data, writing, graphics) for nonprofit educational purposes only, provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigators, awardee organizations, and NIH NIAID are credited. When NIH responds to FOIA requests, material will be subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions to protect confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample has been reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology. If you have trouble accessing the content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) / required application metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must complete SF424 (R&R) items such as type of submission, federal identifier, applicant organization DUNS, legal name, department, address, EIN/TIN, type of applicant, descriptive project title, proposed start and end dates, congressional district, PD/PI contact information, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields shown in the sample include Federal Identifier, Organizational DUNS, EIN/TIN, applicant contact, applicant type, project title, start and end dates, and other SF424-specific required fields. Complete all required SF424 items per the solicitation and form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 components / Table of Contents sections
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete PHS 398 application must include specific attachments and sections (e.g., Project Summary/Abstract, Public Health Relevance Statement, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, Senior/Key Person profiles and biosketches, Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Vertebrate Animals, Bibliography & References Cited, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan, Checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Table of Contents lists these PHS 398-specific sections and attachments; include each relevant section in the order and with the content required by PHS 398 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary / Project Narrative / Public health relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary (abstract) must concisely describe aims, rationale, and expected impact. The Project Narrative (Public Health Relevance Statement) must explain the public health significance of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Project Summary outlines background, knowledge gap (unknown lymphoid signals for stromal growth), overall approach, and expected contribution. The Public Health Relevance Statement links thymic function to immune health and pediatric immunodeficiency relevance. Ensure these sections clearly state significance and relevance in plain language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and demonstrate the adequacy of laboratory, animal, computer, office, core facilities, and the broader scientific environment to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample describes lab square footage, animal facility details (quarantine, BSL3 suite, trained staff and onsite veterinarian), dedicated computers and cluster access, office space and administrative support, and available cores (flow cytometry, proteomics, genomics, screening). Explicitly state access, capabilities, and institutional synergistic environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major equipment listing and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: List dedicated lab equipment and major core instruments relevant to the project, and state whether equipment is readily accessible or restricted to core personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample lists cryostat, fluorescent microscope, centrifuges, tissue culture equipment, FACS Aria sorter (core-run by trained operator), LSR2 cytometer, microarray and bioanalyzer equipment, high-performance computing cluster specs, and multi-TB storage. Indicate access policies (e.g., operator-run, training/fee structure) and that capacity is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch content and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosketch should include name, position/title, eRA Commons user name, education/training, personal statement, positions and employment history, selected peer-reviewed publications, and research support (ongoing and completed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Petrie biosketch provides a personal statement connecting past work to the proposed studies, lists education and training, detailed positions, selected publications with citations, and descriptions of ongoing/completed research support. Follow PHS 398 biosketch format and include items that demonstrate expertise and relevance to the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource/Data sharing plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare how data and resources generated by the project will be shared with the research community, and specify timing and constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample states: data will be shared via peer-reviewed publications; final research data shall be made available no later than acceptance for publication of main findings; TSRI may delay disclosure up to 60 days to exercise IP rights; format/presentation determined later per scientific standards; unique genetic (mouse) resources will be shared per NOT-OD-04-042. Ensure data/resource sharing complies with NIH policy and institutional terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification for use of animals, numbers and statistical/experimental design reasoning, veterinary care, procedures to minimize pain and distress, monitoring, euthanasia methods, and why alternatives are not suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample details: animals must be used because thymic function cannot be recapitulated in vitro; explicit numbers (e.g., total mice requested, breakdown by experiment and replicates), sex selection to minimize variation (males only), breeding numbers, potential reductions by donor reuse, veterinary services, anesthesia agents for procedures (isoflurane, buprenorphine, ketamine/xylazine), monitoring frequency, and euthanasia method (CO2 asphyxiation followed by thoracotomy consistent with AVMA Panel recommendations). Include these elements and justify numbers and procedures per NIH/PHS animal welfare policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal numbers justification and design considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Design experiments with appropriate replication and explicit justification for animal numbers, including time points, biological replicates, pooling strategy, and sex selection to control variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample's Aim 1 design: 5 time points × 3 microarrays each × tissue from three IL7R-/- mice per microarray = 45 mice (but due to using only males actual IL7R-/- mice required = 90 with matched wildtype donors). Preliminary experiments with specified time points and replicates are enumerated; breeding animals and potential additional numbers for validation are estimated. Explain how numbers were derived and opportunities to reduce numbers (e.g., transplant multiple recipients from single donor) and include amendments if numbers change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate prioritization / scoring criteria (bioinformatic and experimental prioritization)
rubrics_metrics.description: When prioritizing candidate stromal receptor:lymphoid ligand pairs, use multifaceted, redundant, and quantitative scoring approaches including dynamic expression patterns, biological plausibility, and statistical metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample specifies prioritization criteria such as dynamic patterns of expression during growth phases, known functional relevance (growth/differentiation/survival) in other tissues, availability of existing genetic models, co-occurrence/thymus/overall scores, and low ANOVA q values. It emphasizes combining quantitative scoring with final qualitative prioritization to select candidates for validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological validation criteria for candidate signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Define clear, testable validation endpoints and genetic approaches for establishing biological relevance of prioritized candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample lists validation strategies: use viable germline or conditional mutant alleles of the lymphoid ligand or stromal receptor; conditional deletions mediated by hCD2[Cre] for lymphoid or Foxn1[Cre] for stromal epithelial cells; expected phenotype is a hypocellular thymus; preferable lymphoid models include transplantation of lineage-negative marrow from mutant mice into IL7R-/- recipients to demonstrate absence of induced growth response. Describe expected outcomes and downstream assays to differentiate effects on proliferation, differentiation, or survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and milestone planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a realistic timeline that allocates time for experimental setup, data collection, analysis/prioritization, and follow-up validation or manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample timeline: first 6-8 months to determine kinetics and perform sample collection; next 6-8 months primarily for data analysis and prioritization; remaining 8-12 months for refining outcomes for publication and preliminary tests of biological relevance. Tie personnel effort and milestones to the timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist and administrative certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS 398-specific checklist items and certifications (application type, inventions and patents disclosure, program income, disclosure permission statement, human subjects/vertebrate animal answers, environmental impact, international activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample repeats SF424 cover page responses on the PHS 398 checklist and requires the authorized representative's signature certifying the statements as true per US Code Title 18 Section 1001. Answer each checklist question fully and attach required documents where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of institutional cores and trained operators (resource access statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If project relies on core facilities, describe instrumentation, operator policies (institutional support, training, fee-for-service), and access (availability, capacity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample describes the Flow Cytometry Core (FACS Aria sorter run by an institutionally-supported, trained operator; directed by the PI), Microarray Core equipment and access rules (some equipment restricted to dedicated core personnel), and Proteomics Core availability. State any limits on access and whether core staff will perform operations or training will be provided.
